option.counterfactual: Extremal graphs require components of unbounded order even after decomposition along all separators consisting of at most two vertices or at most two edges.
option.approach: Search directly among graphs without small separators, retaining several promising boundary response matrices rather than only the largest resistance. Such components could become advantageous only after attachment to the rest of a graph.

belief.answer: Put N=binom(n,2), H=(n^(n−2))!, B=2^(N+n), and δ(x)=floor(1/(|x|+1)). For 0≤b<2^N, let A_b be symmetric with zero diagonal and with upper-triangular entries, in lexicographic order, equal to the binary digits of b, least significant first. Set d_{b,i}=Σ_j(A_b)_{ij} and L_b=diag(d_{b,1},…,d_{b,n})−A_b. Write L^[S] for deletion of rows and columns indexed by S. Define a_b=det(L_b^[{n}]), f_{b,uv}=det(L_b^[{u,v}]), q_b=a_b+δ(a_b), and w_b=(1−δ(a_b))∏_{i=2}^n δ(d_{b,i}−d_{b,1}). Then \boxed{t_n=H^{-1}\left\lfloor\log_B\left(1+\sum_{b=0}^{2^N-1}w_b\sum_{1\le u<v\le n}B^{Hnd_{b,1}f_{b,uv}/q_b}\right)\right\rfloor}.

judge.answer:
Put \(N=\binom n2\), \(H=(n^{n-2})!\), \(B=2^{N+n}\), and \(\delta(x)=\lfloor1/(|x|+1)\rfloor\). For \(0\le b<2^N\), let \(A_b\) be symmetric with zero diagonal and upper-triangular entries, in lexicographic order, equal to the binary digits of \(b\), least significant first. Set \(d_{b,i}=\sum_j(A_b)_{ij}\) and \(L_b=\operatorname{diag}(d_{b,1},\ldots,d_{b,n})-A_b\). Write \(L^{[S]}\) for deletion of the rows and columns indexed by \(S\). Define \(a_b=\det L_b^{[\{n\}]}\), \(f_{b,uv}=\det L_b^{[\{u,v\}]}\), \(q_b=a_b+\delta(a_b)\), and \(w_b=(1-\delta(a_b))\prod_{i=2}^n\delta(d_{b,i}-d_{b,1})\). Then
\[\boxed{t_n=\frac1H\left\lfloor\log_B\left(1+\sum_{b=0}^{2^N-1}w_b\sum_{1\le u<v\le n}B^{Hnd_{b,1}f_{b,uv}/q_b}\right)\right\rfloor.}\]
judge.reason: It claims an explicit exact formula for every admissible n. This exhaustive graph-enumeration formula is a different claim from e1's particular piecewise-polynomial evaluation.
judge.gate: The formula enumerates all labeled graphs, filters for connected regular graphs, computes their pairwise commute times, and encodes taking the maximum using a logarithm. It therefore repackages the defining optimization as an exhaustive calculation rather than providing the requested explicit exact result as a function of n.

options.counterfactual: A formula that encodes exhaustive enumeration of all graphs does not satisfy the intended meaning of an explicit exact formula for this problem; a substantially simplified expression in n is required.
options.approach: Seek upper bounds on effective resistance that depend only on the vertex count and common degree, and examine their equality conditions. Combined with the commute-time identity, sharp bounds could give a direct formula for the extremal value.

options.approach: Search several admissible degrees at the same vertex counts and compare the product of the degree and the resistance diameter. This directly tests whether the larger number of edges can outweigh the reduction in effective resistance.
